review.notes: v1 -> v5 (OP05-EN024, 2017-08-03, the pinned modern text) is codification rather than behaviour change: v2 (HL05-EN006, 2007-12) narrows the lock to 'other monsters', and v3 (BP01-EN042, 2012-05-24) adds '(but you can Set)' - upstream's shared cost already registers EFFECT_CANNOT_SUMMON / EFFECT_CANNOT_FLIP_SUMMON / EFFECT_CANNOT_SPECIAL_SUMMON with an s.sumlimit exemption for Scapegoat's own effect and never blocked Setting, and the GOAT diff does not touch any of it. The second upstream code 511600290 'Scapegoat (Manga)' lives in the unofficial script folder and drops the summon lock entirely (no cost function at all); it is a manga card, not a period TCG version, so it is excluded rather than escalated. Remaining diff is namespacing (id vs MODID for the Sheep Token codes).

event.historical_text: If you activate this card, you cannot Normal Summon, Flip Summon or Special Summon during this turn. Special Summon 4 "Sheep Tokens" (Beast-Type/EARTH/Level 1/ATK 0/DEF 0) in Defense Position to your side of the field. The "Sheep Tokens" cannot be used as a Tribute for a Tribute Summon (or Set).
event.summary: Period activation legality: the GOAT variant maintains its own summon-activity counter (an aux.GlobalCheck block that recomputes Summon + Flip Summon + Special Summon counts at EVENT_CHAIN_END and increments them on the actual EVENT_SUMMON / EVENT_FLIP_SUMMON / EVENT_SPSUMMON events, reset with aux.AddValuesReset) and, whenever Scapegoat is activated while a chain exists (Duel.GetCurrentChain(true)>0), tests that snapshot instead of Duel.GetActivityCount - so Scapegoat can still be chained to an effect that Special Summons (upstream annotation: 'Can be chained to an effect that special summons'), which the modern cost check refuses once the turn has registered such activity. With no chain in progress both scripts require zero Summon, Flip Summon and Special Summon activity for the turn. Chronology unresolved: nothing in the packet dates the change.
